[T-1773] UPSTREAM GAP + fix proposal: dangling PATH symlinks into a framework install are undetected by fw doctor.

WHAT BROKE (ring20-dashboard): /root/.agentic-framework (home-level install) no longer exists. Both global symlinks the framework installs -- ~/.local/bin/fw and ~/.local/bin/claude-fw -- dangled into it. `command -v` SILENTLY SKIPS dangling symlinks, so the symptom is byte-identical to "never installed".

CONSEQUENCE 1 -- misdiagnosis + near-miss duplicate build: our T-1770 ran `command -v claude-fw`, got nothing, concluded "wrapper not on PATH", and scoped a task to BUILD scripts/claude-fw. It avoided shipping a duplicate wrapper only because the agent happened to check .agentic-framework/bin/ first. Luck, not tooling.

CONSEQUENCE 2 -- T-179 continuous mode silently dead: budget-gate.sh kept writing .context/working/.restart-requested with nothing consuming it. Live evidence: signal written 13:48Z, reason=critical_budget_gate_block, tokens=299385, FW_CLAUDE_FW_SUPERVISED unset, unconsumed, aged past the 300s TTL. Zero warning on any surface.

WHY THE FRAMEWORK COULDNT SEE IT: fw doctor validates framework health from INSIDE the project. Nothing inspects the PATH surface -- the surface the operator actually types into. A framework that installs global symlinks has no check that they still resolve.

PROPOSED fw doctor CHECK: for each dir in PATH, `find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -xtype l -printf '%p -> %l\n'`, filter targets matching agentic-framework or /bin/(fw|claude-fw). Report each FAIL with the repoint one-liner `ln -sfn <FRAMEWORK_ROOT>/bin/<name> <link>`. Cheap, zero false positives (a dangling link is unambiguously broken), catches the class not the instance.

OUR FIX (T-1771/T-1772): repointed both at the vendored copy, 2 dangling -> 0. Global-fw sharing verified SAFE: bin/fw:17-24 (T-2450/F3) documents the global symlink as expected deployment, :68-82 resolves PROJECT_ROOT by cwd walk-up. Confirmed live -- fw from a foreign project dir reports Mode: global + that project's root, not ours.

THE WRAPPER ITSELF IS SOUND -- proved by execution, not reading. Harness: throwaway git repo + stub `claude` earlier on PATH so the real restart branch runs. fresh signal -> Auto-restart #1, relaunch with -c, FW_NEXT_DIRECTIVE exported; stale 600s vs 300s TTL -> ignored + cleaned; runaway -> "Max restarts (5) reached" + signal cleared. 3/3. No upstream change needed there.

SECOND FINDING -- FW_CONTEXT_WINDOW defaults to 300000. On 1M-context models the gate declares critical at ~285K, under 30% of the real window. That used to be only warnings; with a WORKING claude-fw it now fires REAL auto-restarts. Consider deriving the window per-model, or making the override far more prominent.

THIRD FINDING (termlink 0.9.0, hit while sending this) -- a hub started via `hub start --tcp` uses runtime_dir /var/lib/termlink, but a stale /tmp/termlink-0/hub.{pid,sock} from an older run SHADOWS it: every local CLI verb (channel.list, agent peers, agent contact) hit the orphaned socket and failed "Connection refused", while hub probe / fleet status / remote list worked fine over TCP. `termlink doctor --fix` cleaned it. Two asks: (a) make a local-hub transport failure distinguishable from a genuine unknown-peer error -- `agent contact framework-agent` reported "session not found ... on any hub" when the real cause was unreachable local state, which sends you hunting the wrong problem; (b) `agent contact <name>` cannot resolve a session that is live and `state: ready` on a hub in hubs.toml unless it is agent-presence registered -- I had to pull identity_fingerprint from `remote status` and use --target-fp. Worth either falling back to session-name resolution across hubs, or saying so in the error.
